f00fde90e3: Created on Yollocalli's original building with Artist Sal Jimenez, this mural is a visual dedication to all immigrants and allies who have stood strong in the face of anti-immigrant rhetoric.

f76b9c3ee3: London-based artist, Ben Eine, uses brightly colored lettering in his signature circus-y font to create his mural, Harmony, stretching 240 feet long and 30 feet tall, with its base starting about 17 feet off the ground.

93d1471f03: Internationally respected DOZE GREEN is the featured artist for the 2012 block-long Glenwood wall from Morse to Farwell. His mural, "The Digital Frontier" relates to the impact of technology on communication and the eternal creating and breaking of boundaries. Doze uses simple graphic imagery combined with complex layering and color movement to show the constant flux of realities, addressing the present moment and connecting it with the past and future. Light beams emanating from individual faces map the manifestation of ideas and the future, and arms are raised for the revolutions and uprisings. Waves show the movement of technology, language and science and windows within windows will represent limitations, barriers, privacy rights and global censorship.
72754d9343: The Undercurrent project brought art and beauty to lower Michigan Avenue with installations from three local artists. The artists were asked to create a “mirror” image of what was above below, and we are amazed by what they created. The installations can be found on the walls at The Realtors Building (Billy Goat Tavern), Intercontinental Hotel, the north wall of Grand Avenue and Michigan Avenue and serve as a brighter and safer route for commuters and visitors walking Lower Michigan Avenue.
a0c08e8da3: Yollocalli students, along with Chucho created a powerful a mural titled, "Wall of Hope" for the local Pilsen organization, San Jose Obrero Mission. The mural displays awareness and commitment to the community.
